samples.summary: The `useState`/`useEffect` → `useQuery` rewrite of `SharedDocumentByToken` — the component that actually delivers the mid-session downgrade this whole change is built around — has no test at all; only the two extracted predicates are covered.
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/api/share-links.test.ts` covers `isRevokedShareLinkError`, `isShareLinkResolveFatal` and `shouldRetryShareLinkResolve` as pure functions. Nothing covers the wiring in `shared-document.tsx`: `enabled: Boolean(token)`, `refetchInterval: SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS`, `retry`, the `token && isLoading` loader branch, the `!token || fatal || !resolved` unavailable branch, or — most importantly — that a re-resolve returning `role: 'viewer'` actually propagates into the `readOnly` prop the docs/notes/slides views consume. The new `*-view-readonly.test.tsx` files prove the views rebuild *when the prop flips*, but nothing proves the prop ever flips. A grep of packages/frontend for `SharedDocumentByToken` finds only `shared-document.tsx`, `App.tsx` and `shared-blob-routing.test.ts` (which does not mount it). If the query wiring is wrong (e.g. the interval never fires, or `isLoading` semantics under `enabled:false` render the wrong branch), the revocation feature is a silent no-op and every test in this PR still passes.

samples.summary: `getStore().setPageSetup()` after `dispose()` — the one member the diff explicitly calls out as "the single page-setup-shaped hole" — is not covered by the new disposed-editor tests.
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/test/view/editor-read-only.test.ts`'s new `a disposed editor is inert` block exercises `insertText`, `deleteBlock` and `doc.insertText` through the stale handles, but never `setPageSetup`. The read-only suite has a dedicated test for that route (`editor-page-setup.test.ts:341`, `editor.getStore().setPageSetup(...)`); the disposal route, which is the change under review (`docStore.setPageSetup` → `revocableStore.setPageSetup`), has none. A regression back to `docStore` would leave a stale holder rewriting page geometry on the shared document with every test still green.

samples.summary: `revocableDocStore`'s non-`get` proxy traps are untested in the revoked state, although the identical traps on `readOnlyDocStore` each have a dedicated escape-route test.
samples.evidence: read-only.ts:206-227 adds revoked-state behaviour for `set`, `defineProperty`, `deleteProperty`, `getPrototypeOf`, `setPrototypeOf`, `preventExtensions`, `has`, `getOwnPropertyDescriptor` and `ownKeys`. `editor-read-only.test.ts` pins every one of these for the read-only handle (the prototype-steal test at ~820, the `preventExtensions` test at 839, the `in` test at 852), but the new `a disposed editor is inert` describe only calls methods. Nothing asserts, e.g., that `Object.getPrototypeOf(staleStore)` is null after dispose, or that `vi.spyOn`-style `defineProperty` is refused — the exact bypasses the read-only work was written for. No dedicated unit test file for `revocableDocStore` exists (grep found it only in src and design docs).

samples.summary: The new `isDisposed()` guard in `insertImageFromUrl` has no test; only the `insertImageFromFile` twin is covered.
samples.evidence: `image-insert.test.ts` adds exactly one disposal test — "inserts nothing when the editor was disposed under the upload" — against `insertImageFromFile`. `insertImageFromUrl` gained the same guard (plus a toast and a `return false`) and is not exercised at all in that file; the file never imports it.

samples.summary: The `insertLink` cell-range test asserts only the undo-stack delta and never that any href was written, unlike every sibling test in the same describe.
samples.evidence: In the new `cell-range writes are one undo unit` describe, `it("insertLink's cell-range arm is one undo unit")` does `const before = …length; editor.insertLink('https://example.com'); expect(length).toBe(before + 1);` — no assertion on the cells' `style.href` and no undo round-trip, where the neighbouring `applyTableCellStyle` test asserts backgrounds before and after undo. The test therefore cannot distinguish "one unit that applied the link to all 64 cells" from a unit that applied it to one cell (or to the wrong slices).

samples.summary: `redo()` discarding the pending checkpoint is asserted only for `undo()`; no test pins the `redo` half of the invariant.
samples.evidence: `memory.test.ts` adds "undo does not apply a checkpoint left pending by a no-op action", which covers `undo()`'s `this.pendingSnapshot = null`. The symmetric line in `redo()` has no test that would fail if it were removed: the only snapshot-then-redo case ("an action that snapshots but writes nothing costs no undo unit") asserts the redone text, which holds either way — the divergence only shows on the *next* write, where a stale pending checkpoint would make undo jump back past the redo.
searchedFor: read the memory.test.ts hunks in the diff

samples.summary: `setDocument()` / `replaceDocument()` newly call `willWrite()` (materializing a pending checkpoint and clearing redo), and no test covers that side effect.
samples.evidence: The pre-existing tests at memory.test.ts:100 ("replaceDocument syncs without pushing undo") and :110/:142 pass unchanged because they have no redo stack and no pending checkpoint. Nothing asserts the new behaviour: that `replaceDocument`/`setDocument` now drop redo history, or that a `snapshot(); setDocument(...)` sequence materializes the checkpoint via `willWrite` rather than via the old code path. A regression that dropped `willWrite()` from these two mutators would leave a stale redo entry applicable over a freshly loaded document, undetected.

samples.summary: `withUndoUnit`'s documented "held renders are replayed once, including after a throw" is only tested on the success path.
samples.evidence: The doc comment on `withUndoUnit` claims the deferred `requestRender()` replays "at most once — after the outermost unit commits, including after a throw". The only test is `editor-undo-selection.test.ts`'s "paints once for the whole action, after the unit commits" (`ctxCalls.save === 1`) on a normal typing path. No test drives a body that throws, so the `finally`-based replay (and the `renderAfterUndoUnit` reset that prevents a stuck flag across later units) is unexercised — a stuck flag would leave the editor painting stale content after a partial write.
searchedFor: read editor-undo-selection.test.ts paint-count test in diff

samples.summary: `YorkieDocStore.dispose()` has no direct unit test (idempotency, clearing `onRemoteChange`), while the mirror-image `YorkieNoteStore.dispose()` got one.
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/app/notes/yorkie-note-store.test.ts` adds "releases its document subscription on dispose" including an idempotency assertion. verdict.reason: Verified independently: no test in the repository mounts `SharedDocumentByToken` or exercises its useQuery wiring. A repo-wide grep for `SharedDocument|shared-document` across packages/frontend yields only App.tsx:18 (route registration), template-landing.tsx:174 and template-review-queue.tsx:136 (production callers), shared-blob-routing.test.ts:2 (imports only the pure `sharedBlobKind`), and template-review-queue.test.tsx:30-31, which explicitly `vi.mock`s the module away and substitutes a stub. public-templates.test.tsx:51-61 does render `App` under MemoryRouter but only routes /templates, /t:id (stubbed div) and /login, so it never mounts the shared route. share-links.test.ts (read in full) covers isRevokedShareLinkError / isShareLinkResolveFatal / shouldRetryShareLinkResolve as pure functions and states at lines 61-65 that it deliberately avoids mounting the component. The three *-view-readonly.test.tsx files drive `readOnly` via `view.rerender` with a literal boolean (docs-view-readonly.test.tsx:126-144), proving the views rebuild when the prop flips but never that the re-resolve makes it flip. No frontend e2e layer exists (`**/e2e/**` matches nothing; backend *.e2e-spec.ts are Nest HTTP tests), and no test file anywhere mentions `refetchInterval` or the "Link unavailable" copy. So the loader branch (`token && isLoading`), the unavailable branch, `enabled: Boolean(token)`, the 60s `refetchInterval`, and — most importantly — propagation of a re-resolved `role: 'viewer'` into the `readOnly` prop consumed at shared-document.tsx:198/339/401/428/716 are untested. Under the test-adequacy rubric this is a missing test over a change whose failure silently weakens a client-side authority guard and makes the revocation/downgrade feature a no-op with every test in the change still green: major.
